request.rationale: M7 shows that T1's residual failures are negative-angle open-branch acquisition failures with negative joint-limit margin, while the late latched remap in T7 was rejected because it changed branch semantics only near the target and disrupted approach dynamics. This narrower policy-only intervention commits from the first observation whenever geometry proves the open posture infeasible, without changing torques or the learned action path after commitment. Transfer preserves T1's broad approach and hold competence; the bounded adaptation tests whether consistent feasible-branch semantics repair the diagnosed failures without increasing failures elsewhere. Require paired complete-hold improvement over T1 on the shared diagnostic panel before assigning any role.

request.description: Run paired 160-episode research evaluations of T8:checkpoint-5120, T8:checkpoint-10240, T8:checkpoint-35840, and T1:checkpoint-100352 on shared episode seeds 4200-4359. Record complete uninterrupted hold success plus reach, first-entry, longest-hold, residual-motion, branch, posture, joint-limit, conditioning, interruption, and target-geometry diagnostics.
request.rationale: T8 transfer training preserves T1-level training-stream success at checkpoints 5120 and 10240, remains near it at 35840, and degrades at later checkpoints. Training success and shaped reward are not evidence of official complete-hold performance. Evaluating the two strongest early checkpoints and the later near-peak checkpoint against T1 on identical seeds is the highest-value test of whether static geometry-gated feasible-branch semantics repair negative-angle failures, whether the effect is transient, and whether approach and hold behavior remain intact. No candidate role will be assigned without paired complete-hold improvement and diagnostic evidence.

request.reason: M8 measured T8:checkpoint-5120 at 159/160 complete-hold successes (99.375%), improving on T1's 151/160 with 9 candidate wins versus 1 reference win and a +5.0 percentage-point paired delta. It is tied with T8:checkpoint-10240 on outcome but uses the least adaptation, preserving the transferred T1 behavior most conservatively while correcting the diagnosed infeasible open-branch failures. No official assessment has yet been requested.

request.candidates_and_roles: T8:checkpoint-5120 is the best-known candidate, assigned by E14, with M8 evidence at 159/160 complete-hold successes and model fingerprint 85497cedbc3b398c33a5212b7f8bab501e6957f8eb8e83edcc77a6d90026928f. T8:checkpoint-10240 is an equal-outcome unassigned alternative; T8:checkpoint-35840 and T1 remain unassigned or superseded. No official candidate role is assigned.
request.cumulative_resource_use: T1 used one fresh 100352-step PPO training operation and baseline panels M1/M7; T2/M2, T3/M3, T4/M4, T5/M5, and T6/M6 tested and rejected reward, observation, distribution, curriculum, and action-path alternatives. E7, E9, and E10 restored T1 between lines. E13 restored T1 before T8. T7 used one 100352-step transfer-training operation and M7 evaluated its early and terminal checkpoints. T8 used one 50000-step transfer-training operation and M8 evaluated three T8 checkpoints plus T1 on the shared 160-episode panel. No official benchmark assessment has yet been requested.
request.current_goal_gap: T8:checkpoint-5120 is the best-known candidate at 159/160 (99.375%) on the shared 160-episode panel, with 9 candidate wins versus 1 T1 reference win and a +5.0 percentage-point success delta. This exceeds the projected 98% research threshold, but official success is still unknown because the protected assessment uses a distinct 200-episode panel. T8:checkpoint-10240 ties this result; T8:checkpoint-35840 achieves 157/160.
request.current_synthesis: M1 and M7 establish that T1 failures were dominated by policy-controlled acquisition of an infeasible open-branch posture for negative-angle targets: six failures never entered tolerance and three held only 1-2 checks, all with negative minimum joint-limit margin, while no failures were caused by later hold interruption. M8 shows that a static geometry-gated observation-only remap, applied from the initial observation only when open is infeasible and folded is feasible, repairs this mechanism without changing reward, target distribution, observation size, or direct torque realization: T8:checkpoint-5120 reaches 159/160 and wins 9 of 10 discordant episodes against T1. The late remap in T7 and direct action correction in T6 remain rejected; the evidence supports feasible-branch policy semantics, not forced physical posture control.
request.decision_frontier: Accept T8:checkpoint-5120 as the best-known research candidate and reject T7 and the other tested interventions as improvements. I1's closure condition is met: the baseline has decomposition by reach, first entry, longest hold, residual motion, branch/posture, and target geometry, and M8 supports one actionable intervention with paired improvement and no observed broad degradation. Do not claim the human goal is met until the protected 200-episode official assessment is executed.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. M8 measured the best T8 candidate at 159/160 (99.375%) on the complete-hold research panel, exceeding the research threshold and providing a credible frozen policy for official assessment, while the official 200-episode result remains unmeasured.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Close I1 in the next inquiry session because its stated behavioral closure condition is satisfied. Then, with no active inquiry and T8:checkpoint-5120 explicitly best-known, request the protected official assessment. Treat the official 200-episode result as the only evidence of reaching the human goal; if it is below 196/200, reopen scientific work rather than treating the research-panel result as sufficient.
